title: Napock (Peconic River Headwaters)
summary: Napock is connected with the Peconic River headwaters, a chain of ponds and wetlands along the Riverhead/Brookhaven boundary. The history preserves a boundary placename tied to water, pools, and the interior landscape of central Long Island. The name is interpreted as a water-place or pool-place.
map_geometry_source: approximate Peconic Lake / Forge Pond marker for Peconic River headwaters; not exact historical coordinate
history_content: Napock is best treated as a boundary-and-waterbody placename rather than a single exact point. Time-specific land and boundary context is handled in the Historic Moments section.
translation_content:
Napock is related to forms such as Nipock and is analyzed from elements meaning water and land or place. The resulting interpretation is water-place or pool-place, matching the ponded headwaters setting.

Why Place Names Matter

“Knowing traditional place names helps connect and identify locations from oral stories or written history of ancestors and the traditional lifestyle.”

— Tim Malchoff and Kari Brookover for Chugachmiut Heritage Preservation, Traditional Place Names (n.d.), Traditional Place Names Overview, final sentence
whereintheworld_content: The map placement uses Peconic Lake/Forge Pond in Calverton as a modern reference for the Peconic River headwaters.
